mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (indicating accommodative monetary policy) compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds across all monetary regimes as the rate level is a direct proxy for policy stance.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between FEDFUNDS level and 20-day S&P 500 returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0% is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (below 4.0%) signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day S&P 500 return when UNRATE is below 4.0% is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High levels of both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL > 250) indicate a restrictive monetary policy environment combined with elevated inflation, which suppresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day S&P 500 return when both FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 250 is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC for the interaction term is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, strong retail sales (RSAFS > 500,000 million dollars) signal robust consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day S&P 500 return when RSAFS > 500,000 million dollars in late-cycle expansions is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of industrial production (above 107) signals robust manufacturing activity and economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day S&P 500 return when INDPRO > 107 is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) signals strong demand for residential construction, which supports economic growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between HOUST level and 20-day S&P 500 returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return when HOUST is above its 5-year median is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong job growth (PAYEMS > 150,000 thousand) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) signals a tight labor market, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day S&P 500 return when PAYEMS > 150000 and UNRATE < 4.0% is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC for the interaction term is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 250) signals the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day S&P 500 return when CPIAUCSL > 250 is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
